Forecast Discussion

A strong low pressure has developed off the southern New England coast. The cyclonic flow around the low is bringing cold air from Canada across the Great Lakes into the southern Appalachians. The cold moist flow is lifted by the mountains creating occasional snow showers and flurries today. The frequency and intensity of the snow showers increases this afternoon and overnight as upper level energy rotates around the low. Greatest accumulations will be in the higher peaks near the TN border with lesser accumulations in the valleys and near the Blue Ridge.

Temperatures are about 15 degrees below average today and combined with gusty winds, it will feel bitterly cold; especially since we have been in a mild stretch for good while prior to this cold snap.

The low begins to move far enough away on Saturday that the snow shower activity winds down during the morning. Snow showers linger the longest across the western mountains near the TN border. Saturday continue to be cold and windy though.

High pressure builds in Sunday and is nearly overhead Monday and Tuesday. This allows the wind to decrease and afternoon temperatures to warm. Morning temperatures remain cold as the winds go calm and combined with clear skies and dry air, temperatures drop off rapidly overnight.

Wednesday and Thursday continue the warming trend as temperatures get to near and slightly above average.

After precipitation ends Saturday, it appears western NC goes into another long stretch of dry weather.
